SpatialCopyInference

SpatialCopyInference infers chromosome arm-level somatic copy number aberrations (SCNAs) directly from Xenium spatial transcriptomics data. The package identifies and spatially maps SCNA-defined cell populations through spatial clustering and provides downstream tools for visualisation, differential expression analysis, pathway enrichment and identification of genes and genomic regions associated with inferred SCNAs. SpatialCopyInference enables the study of tumour evolution and early cancer development in situ.

Documentation, including the entire workflow using a human ovarian cancer dataset, is available here.

A companion website containing analyses supporting the study is available at SpatialCopyInference-paper.

You can read more about SpatialCopyInference in our preprint.

Installation

You can install SpatialCopyInference with the following command:

remotes::install_github("florishonig/SpatialCopyInference")

Example workflow

A minimum workflow is shown below:

# Import data
xenium.obj <- import_xenium(data_dir, annotation_file)

# Quality control
xenium.obj <- filter_cells(xenium.obj)
xenium.obj <- filter_genes(xenium.obj)

# Normalisation
xenium.obj <- normalise_data(xenium.obj)

# SCNA inference
arm_means <- compute_arm_means(xenium.obj)
arm_ratios <- compute_arm_ratios(arm_means, xenium.obj)

# Spatial clustering
BANKSY.obj <- compute_spatial_clusters(arm_ratios, xenium.obj)

xenium.obj <- add_banksy_clusters(xenium.obj, BANKSY.obj)

# Visualisation
plot_cluster_heatmaps(BANKSY.obj)
plot_spatial_clusters(xenium.obj)

# Downstream analyses
cluster_results <- compare_spatial_clusters(xenium.obj, ident_1 = "1", ident_2 = "2")
plot_gene_density(de_results = cluster_results$de)
gene_clusters <- identify_gene_clusters(de_results = cluster_results$de)
plot_gene_clusters(gene_clusters = gene_clusters)
